sources.entry: Safebucket - File sharing platform with pluggable infrastructure, where uploads and downloads go directly between clients and S3-compatible storage. (Source Code) Apache-2.0 Go/Docker

summary.one_liner: Safebucket is an open source file sharing platform with pluggable infrastructure where files go directly between clients and storage via presigned URLs, bypassing the server.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes direct uploads and downloads through presigned URLs so files bypass the server. Every component (storage, database, events, cache, notifier) is described as swappable. It supports SSO via any OIDC provider with local auth for external users, and role-based access control at platform and bucket level. Users can create quick or reverse shares as public links with options such as password, max downloads, and max views. It also lists real-time activity tracking, audit logs, TOTP multifactor authentication, file expiration, a trash with configurable retention, and an admin dashboard with platform-wide statistics.
use_cases: share files with external users via public links
self-hosted file transfer with S3-compatible storage
collect files from others via reverse share
audit file access in a team bucket
time-limited file expiration with trash retention
how_to_run: Open the web UI and log in with admin@safebucket.io / ChangeMePlease (change this password)
For external access, set STORAGE__RUSTFS__EXTERNAL_ENDPOINT, APP__ALLOWED_ORIGINS, APP__API_URL and APP__WEB_URL in the .env file to your host IP or domain
notable: Files bypass the server via presigned URLs for direct client-to-storage transfer
Every component (storage, database, events, cache, notifier) is swappable
Quick and reverse share links with password, max downloads, and max views
Container images are signed with cosign keyless signing through GitHub Actions OIDC
Local quick start uses docker compose with a RustFS storage endpoint
caveats: The quick start uses a default admin password that must be changed
External access requires manually editing several environment variables in .env
README does not state platform support or production hardening guidance beyond the local lite deployment
